summary: Envoy's interest reaper deletes a dead session's interest row only when now - UpdatedAt > graceWindow + store.InterestRefreshAge (5 min); the listener passes store.InterestReapGrace (10 min), so 15 minutes since the row's last write. Heartbeat writes do not change. Design source: INFRA-514 plan, T4 step 1.

productionCheck.listeners: Three listeners reap the shared envoy_interests bucket: Dispatch's in-cluster listener (machine id dispatch), gke, and the NATS hub's own listener (envoy-hub). Evidence: the deployment repository's envoy/Pulumi.prod.yaml hosts list (dispatch, legion-daemon with no listener, gke; a person's device has no NATS user), and GET $ENVOY_URL/v1/interests/ machine ids on 2026-10-27: envoy-hub 367, gke 224.
productionCheck.carriesTheMerge: The image's org.opencontainers.image.revision is the merge or a descendant: gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/compare/<merge>...<revision> --jq .status answers identical or ahead. Read a digest's revision with curl and jq: anonymous token from https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:sjawhar/legion/envoy:pull, the index at /v2/sjawhar/legion/envoy/manifests/<digest>, its amd64 manifest, that manifest's config blob, .config.Labels["org.opencontainers.image.revision"] (run 2026-10-27: Dispatch listener sha256:033d1852... reads 35efd326).
steps: Reach the deploy: in the first look, envoy_publish to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-514-architect, expects_reply none (the spec says to route the pin moves through INFRA-514's architect to the controller): the merge commit, the envoy image digest built from it, the three pins in the deployment repository (dispatch/ envoyImage, envoy-cluster/ envoyImage, envoy/ listenerImage), and that moving the hub's listenerImage replaces the hub VM and stops NATS for the swap (packages/envoy/infra/docs/nats-hub.md:496-525).

Read each listener. Dispatch's: kubectl -n dispatch get pods (allowed), the dispatch-listener-* pod's envoy-listener imageID, then its revision; read the pod, not the pin (2026-10-27: pin built from 8f3d4237, running listener 35efd326). gke: kubectl -n envoy get pods -l app=envoy-listener the same way once INFRA-14's grant lands (forbidden today); meanwhile read the envoy-cluster pin on the deployment repository's main with gh api contents and record the running build as not readable. envoy-hub: a pod cannot read the VM; read the envoy/ listenerImage pin and record the running build as not readable.

Only once every listener reads as carrying the merge: run reap-probe.sh (from dispatch doc-read --issue INFRA-610 --artifact reap-probe-sh) against $ENVOY_URL with $ENVOY_TOKEN_FILE; about 25 minutes.

pass: every listener carries the merge and both probe ids read 'new rule'; write the PR's Production: line and one PR comment (each listener's digest and revision or 'pin only', the probe table, merge commit, wake). pending: a listener lacks the merge; Production: stays 'pending deploy of <merge sha>'. fail: all carry the merge but a probe id reads 'old rule'; dispatch ask on the controller's report issue per findings.md, its reference to the controller topic, named in the Production: line.
Then envoy_publish the verdict and the Production: line to INFRA-514's architect, expects_reply none: INFRA-514's tester gates its review on this record.

findings.finding: The spec names three listeners but the repository describes other listener runtimes (on-prem fleet, Fargate); the root's write-skip is safe only if every listener on the shared bucket reaps at 15 minutes.
findings.answer: Measured: the hub's NATS hosts are dispatch, legion-daemon (no listener) and gke, a person's device has no NATS user, and the bucket's rows carry only envoy-hub and gke machine ids. Three listeners reap it. The production probe also measures the rule in force across every listener on the bucket.

findings.finding: From a worker pod the envoy-hub build cannot be read, the gke build is forbidden until INFRA-14's grant, and a pin read is not a running-build read; nothing wakes the check after a pin move.
findings.answer: Dispatch's listener is read from its running pod; gke and envoy-hub from their pins plus the probe, recorded as 'pin only'. Recorded as spec departure 2 for the architect to decide, and the missing wake is a named risk for whoever moves the pins.

findings.finding: The draft probe (present at 14:45, absent at 21:00) cannot tell the old rule from the new one.
findings.answer: Replaced by polling every 5 s to the first 404 with A >= 14:50 and B <= 21:00 for 'new rule', B <= 14:40 for 'old rule', two ids 150 s apart so no single old-rule tick can pass both, 503 counted as unknown, skew measured, cleanup on interruption.
